B2.definition: a person who informs on a person or organization engaged in illicit activity
B2.example: The courageous whistleblower exposed corporate corruption despite receiving threats of immediate job loss.

C1.definition: Feeling or showing anger or annoyance at what is perceived as unfair or unjust treatment.
C1.example: Citizens were indignant when investigative reporters exposed widespread corruption among high-ranking municipal officials governing public funds.

C2.definition: A passage or remark that departs from the main subject in speech or writing; a temporary detour in discourse.
C2.example: After a lengthy historical digression regarding nineteenth-century trade routes, the lecturer returned to the primary topic of contemporary economics.
